subject: Rev: Order Form SLA & Support Redlines — next steps and escalation playbook
messages:
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@cloudwave.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.com, Samir Reddy <samir.reddy@cloudwave.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft Order Form + SLA redlines (CloudWave)

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our updated Order Form with redlines focused on support windows, credit caps, and response definitions. High level asks from CloudWave:

- 99.95% target for production endpoints across the US region (they want hourly measurement).
- 12% service credit per 30 min of downtime beyond the threshold, capped at 50% per month.
- 15 minute response for P1 incidents, 4 hours for P2.
- Maintenance windows: prefer 2 x 6-hour monthly windows with minimum 14 days notice and no more than one per week.

We appreciate the flexibility on dedicated capacity — procurement will need final language on credit calculation and definition of "Downtime" vs "Degraded". Can your legal team review the redlines and propose alternative wording where needed?

Attaching: CloudWave_OrderForm_v3.docx (redlines)

Looking for a 30 minute sync tomorrow to resolve a couple of open items before we escalate internally.

Best,
Erin
Erin Walsh
Director, Cloud Procurement
CloudWave Inc.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Draft Order Form + SLA redlines (CloudWave)

On Tue, Apr 27, 2026 at 09:12 AM Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@cloudwave.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our updated Order Form with redlines focused on support windows, credit caps, and response definitions.

Erin — thanks for sending. We've reviewed the high-level asks and want to propose a pragmatic path forward so we can keep the deal moving without risking operations. Key points from our side:

1) Uptime measurement: we measure availability at the model endpoint level per region in 5-minute buckets. We can commit to 99.95% monthly for production endpoints but need to clarify measurement windows (monthly rolling). Hourly measurement is noisy and will create dispute trees.

2) Service credits: the 12% per 30-min bucket with 50% cap is aggressive. Our standard is 10% per 30-60 min increment with a 30% monthly cap for first-year enterprise customers. We're willing to do a stepped approach: 10% (30-60m), 15% (60-180m), capped at 40% month.

3) Response times: For P1 we can commit to an initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes for customers with Dedicated or Enterprise Support add-on. Hosted customers on standard support have a 60 minute target for P1 acknowledgement. If CloudWave is finalizing to purchase the enterprise support bundle, we can match 15 min.

4) Maintenance windows: we can support up to 2 x 6 hour maintenance windows per month with 14 days' notice; however we need a carveout for emergency maintenance (with immediate notification and post-mortem). Also propose a blackout: no scheduled maintenance during CloudWave major release windows (customer will supply calendar).

Next steps proposed:
- Legal (cc: Karthik) to prepare tracked-change language for "Downtime" (total loss of inference response) vs "Degraded" (increased latency or partial error rate).
- Ops (cc: Laura) to scope what a 15 m P1 acknowledgement means on our oncall rota and whether Dedicated pool guarantees require capacity reservation.
- Set a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:30am PT to align and capture concessions.

I'm attaching an annotated summary (SLA_summary.xlsx) with the suggested compromise table.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.com
Attachment: SLA_summary.xlsx (table of suggested credit tiers)

Priyom — quick operational notes to bring to the call:

- If we agree to the stepped credit approach (10/15), we should tie the cap to a monthly spend floor (e.g., credits capped at 40% but not to exceed 2x monthly committed spend) to avoid open-ended liability.
- Recommend we insist on "acknowledgement" vs "initial remediation" wording for P1 — acknowledgement is achievable; full remediation window depends on incident.
- For maintenance windows we can accept 2x6h/month but request that no more than one window falls on a weekday peak (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 PT) unless customer approves.

I'll take the operational action to prepare suggested language for the credit cap and forward it to Karthik/legal before the 10:30am sync.

-Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@cloudwave.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form + SLA redlines (CloudWave)

Thanks all — quick legal POV after reviewing CloudWave_OrderForm_v3 and Priyom's summary:

- Define terms clearly: "Downtime" = "unavailable to service requests across all replicas in the specified region"; "Degraded" = "requests are returned but 50%+ of requests exceed the configured latency threshold or error rate exceeds 5% over a 5-minute rolling window." This avoids ambiguity during measurement disputes.
- Service credit calculation: replace percentage-per-30min language with a formula tied to "Monthly Service Fee" to keep math auditable. e.g., Credit = min((Downtime_minutes / Total_minutes_in_month) * 100, CreditCap%) * MonthlyServiceFee. Use tiered CreditCap% (10%/15% etc.). This prevents stacks of credits to exceed commensurate spend.
- Response SLA: legal is fine with an "acknowledgement" target of 15 minutes for P1 when enterprise support is procured. Do NOT commit to time-to-resolution in the contract — we should keep root-cause resolution and remediation details in an ops runbook referenced but not embedded in the MSA.
- Maintenance: Agree to 2 windows/month with 14 days notice. Add emergency maintenance carveout with requirement for a written post-mortem within 72 hours and a service-impact classification. Also add language: "No more than one scheduled maintenance event may occur during customer-designated major release weeks (customer to provide calendar at least 30 days in advance)."

I've prepared tracked changes and attached it as SLA_redlines_v2.docx — it includes the formula examples and proposed definitive terms. I recommend we share the tracked doc with CloudWave procurement and offer one round of legal-to-legal redlines, followed by an Ops call to lock instrumentation and measurement.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Dir., Contracts & Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Erin — thanks for the patience and the team for fast turn. Summary and immediate next steps: 

1) Legal will send SLA_redlines_v2.docx to CloudWave procurement with a short cover note outlining the formula approach and definitions for Downtime/Degraded (Karthik to send before EOD PT).
2) Ops (Laura) and I will prepare a short instrumentation note describing how we measure availability (5-minute buckets, regional aggregation) and what logs/metrics we can provide for audit (link to Confluence in the doc).
3) Commercial ask: we propose the stepped credit approach as the base (10%/15%), a 40% monthly cap, and a safeguard limiting credits to a maximum of 2x the monthly committed spend. Marissa will share suggested wording.
4) Sync scheduled: Fri Apr 30, 10:30am PT (30 min) — tentative meeting invite to follow. Please confirm availability.

If CloudWave is comfortable with legal-to-legal exchange + one operational call, we can aim to get final sign-off and a DocuSign loop next week.
